grades.quote: `SC.REL` instruction will write the flag of success or failure of its execution (which can be simply understood as the LLbit value seen by the `SC.REL` instruction when it is executed) into the general-purpose register rd and return it, regardless of whether it writes to the memory or not.
grades.reason: Covers LL.ACQ/SC.REL, the acquire/release variants, not LL.W/SC.W. It describes the same LLbit mechanism: SC.REL writes only if LLbit is 1, returns a success flag in rd, and LLbit is cleared by ERTN or another core's store to the cache line. This is useful as an analogy but does not directly answer the question about SC.W.
Table of contents entries only. They give no information about why SC.W fails or what its result means.

grades.quote: In order to construct this loop, the `SC.[W/D]` instruction will write the flag of its execution success (or simply the `LLbit` value seen when the `SC` instruction is executed) into the general register `rd` and return.
grades.reason: Directly answers the question for LoongArch LL.W/SC.W. SC writes only if LLbit is 1. ERTN (without KLO set) or another core or coherent I/O master storing to the monitored cache line clears LLbit, which makes SC fail. The SC result in rd is the success flag, which is the LLbit value seen, and software uses it to retry the loop.
Describes an RISC-V operational memory model transition for an early sc failure. The query requires LoongArch, so this is the wrong ISA.
